ns2:course.label: Human Osteology
ns2:course.description: Identification of isolated and fragmentary skeletal remains; study of the structure and function of bone, the growth and development of the human skeleton and introduction to analytical techniques used in human osteology including paleopathology, paleodemography and forensics. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. Prerequisite: ANTH 102 or ANTH 240 or a course in anatomy, physiology, or introductory life sciences and consent of instructor.
